chunks: He gave you whatsoever you asked. If you try to count the favours of God you will not be able to calculate. Man is most unjust indeed, full of ingratitude.
ai.seo_question: What does the Quran say about human gratitude and God's favors?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often linked to the concept of 'Tawassul' and divine responsiveness, emphasizing that God grants not just basic needs but every specific request made by the faithful. The description of humans as 'ظَلُومٌ کَفَّارٌ' (unjust and ungrateful) reflects the dual nature of humanity: capable of recognizing blessings yet prone to neglecting them due to ego, a theme central to the Imams' teachings on gratitude (Shukr). This underscores the necessity of conscious appreciation to maintain the flow of divine favors.
